newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES MIXED IN TUESDAY'S MARKET.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES MIXED IN TUESDAY'S MARKET.

text.p: HARARE, July 8 (Reutetr) - Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted mixed in fairly brisk business on Tuesday, dealers said.

They said the market opened with a surplus of Z$92 million and the central Reserve Bank, forecasting another end-of-day surplus of Z$282 million on the back of treasury bill maturities, auctioned 91-day treasury bills worth Z$300 million at 25 percent, up from 24.94 percent the previous day.
Meanwhile, treasury bills were also trading on the secondary market at 24.75 percent from Monday's 24.80 percent and call money eased to 24 from 24.5 percent.

NCD bills redeemable after 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought unchanged at 27 percent but sold at 25.25 percent, marginally down from 25.5 percent. Bank acceptance bills held steady at 26 percent (buying) and at 24.85 percent (selling).
